turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Meredith Kalinowski. I have a call at 4:40, so we have until then. Who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone in the middle of class?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No. You haven't answered me, Hale, and the clock is running.
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Don't manage me, Hale. Your favourite student got a zero without anyone calling his mother, so what do you actually have?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.
Not perfect. That's a machine's guess, Hale, and your own procedure 4.3 says software alone does not establish a concern, so what else is there, or is that it?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.

I'm writing that down: 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Students paste in drafts they wrote somewhere else, Hale, and you haven't shown me a date or put the document in front of me. None of it explains why that zero went in before anyone picked up a phone and called me.
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Save it, Hale. Show me the document with its date on it, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not grading you, Hale. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and nothing touches his record, unless you put that document on the table right now.
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.

I'm writing down exactly what you said: "Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings." Students misremember lines and paraphrase all the time, Hale, so show me the page of Owen's essay where it appears and how he cited it. Then hand me a copy of the play.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.

October 15, I have that down. Writers change direction between an outline and a final draft, Hale, and "completely different" is your word, not a document. Put the outline next to the essay, with that line marked, and let me read them myself.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? Ten minutes, Hale. The outline and the essay, side by side.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.

A rewrite for what, Hale, when you've described documents and still haven't shown me a single one? Agreeing to that now would be admitting something, and I'm not. If you're talking about 4.4, I want it in writing: private, its mark replaces the zero, and nothing ever goes on his file.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
You're asking me how to talk to your own student, Hale? You talk to Owen after I've seen the outline and the essay, not before.
